- Pricing: I attached our suggested private-offer pricing spreadsheet (Redwood_PrivOffer_Pricing_v3.xlsx) with two commitment tiers:

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa — can you confirm marketplace packaging and whether AWS needs any extra metadata for the private offer (pricing tiers, SKU mapping)?

Thanks — Sergio

Hi Sergio / Alicia — happy to help. Quick notes on AWS Marketplace private-offer mechanics:

- Term length: AWS supports custom term lengths on private offers; 12 months is standard and will be displayed in the offer. Reminder: buyer acceptance typically happens in the buyer console unless the buyer prefers to sign a separate PO.
- Approvals: For corporate buyers like MediTech, the procurement team usually requires a PO + acceptance in the console. For speed, we can do the private offer in the console and have the buyer sign a separate PO (your legal) — both are valid.
- Pricing visibility: The buyer will see the private offer price and term in their console; if you want to require DocuSign signature in addition to console acceptance, that needs to be coordinated outside AWS and referenced in your contract.
- Marketplace metadata: please include SKU IDs and the AWS product code in the offer. Also set the offer ID as an internal reference in the PO so we can reconcile.

I’ll create the initial private-offer record using the pricing spreadsheet values you provided and mark the offer in the console as pending until we confirm the buyer email for acceptance.

Jacob Liu
AWS Marketplace Partnerships
AWS
